papers.title: Risk-Aware Self-Play Reinforcement Learning for Secure and Capable Code-Generating Agents
papers.summary: Abstract We study risk-aware self-play in finite-action code repair, separating functional success from test-integrity and forbidden-call violations. From 591 MBPP/HumanEval programs, 395 mutation tasks yield 4,527 candidates. On 133 external HumanEval tasks, the full policy reduces expected violations from 68.55% to 0.64% versus public-test-only RL, but fixed multiobjective rewards achieve slightly higher joint success, 72.78% versus 72.37%. papers.title: A neural circuit mediating altitude control in Drosophila
papers.summary: Flight is a remarkably efficient mode of locomotion that is largely responsible for the extraordinary evolutionary radiations of birds, bats, pterosaurs, and insects. Whereas walking animals need only control locomotion on a two-dimensional surface, flight requires active altitude regulation, a process by which the brain transforms self-motion cues into motor patterns that regulate lift. papers.title: Robotic arm-assisted droplet-based additive manufacturing via acoustic levitation: process implementation and experimental optimization
papers.summary: Abstract This paper presents the concept, implementation and process optimization of a robotic arm-assisted additive manufacturing system using acoustic levitation for droplet-based deposition of photocurable resin. By integrating acoustic levitation and robotic manipulation, the tank-free material deposition approach has the potential to overcome the limitations inherent in conventional 3D printing - such as fixed build directions, planar layers and the reliance on resin tanks. papers.title: KYNEMA: Design and Validation of Multi-Modal Robot Interaction for XR-Based Robotics Education
papers.summary: Hands-on interaction with robots is valuable for robotics education, but hardware access is limited by cost, laboratory capacity, and safety, and 2D interfaces poorly represent real workspaces. We developed a browser-native extended reality (XR) application that displays laboratory robots at true scale in the user's environment and offers three manipulation modes: direct joint control, forward-kinematics control, and inverse-kinematics teleoperation. papers.title: Model & Locomotion Dynamics of a Goat Bio-Inspired Quadruped Robot Through Reinforcement Learning
papers.summary: Traditional control methods struggle to handle high-degree-of-freedom systems and the unpredictability of real-world dynamics. Deep Reinforcement Learning has emerged to overcome this limitation, becoming central to autonomous robotic control and enabling greater agility and adaptability in legged robots. A custom 12-DOF goat-inspired quadruped was trained via PPO-based imitation learning against a reference trajectory built from real ovine motion-capture data. papers.title: Comparison of joint laxity measured using 60- and 80-N distraction forces and manual stress during robot-assisted total knee arthroplasty
papers.summary: BACKGROUND: Appropriate intraoperative soft-tissue balance is essential for achieving successful outcomes following total knee arthroplasty (TKA). However, the optimal distraction force for evaluating joint laxity remains unclear. This study aimed to compare joint laxities measured using specific distraction forces with those obtained under manual varus-valgus stress and assess the interobserver variability. papers.title: Multiphysics Assessment of a Frameless PMSM for Humanoid Robot Joints: Baseline Results and a Roadmap Toward an IPM-SynRM
papers.summary: Frameless torque motors are attractive for humanoid and collaborative robot joints because the stator and rotor can be integrated directly into the load-bearing structure, thereby combining a compact axial envelope, low rotor inertia, and a hollow passage for cables or cooling. This study develops and applies a coupled electromagnetic, thermal, and structural workflow to an 18-slot/20-pole frameless permanent-magnet synchronous motor supplied from a 48 V DC bus and rated at 460 W, 1.75 N·m, and 2500 rpm. papers.title: Design and Experimental Validation of an Underactuated Anthropomorphic Robotic Hand Based on the Ball-Ring-Elliptical Mechanism
papers.summary: This work reports the fabrication and experimental characterization of an underactuated anthropomorphic hand based on the Ball-Ring-Elliptical (BRE) rigid-soft finger of Zhang et al., originally validated on a single multi-material PolyJet prototype. The BRE equations were reconstructed in parametric CAD and printed at several scales on commodity printers, yielding four flexion-only fingers, each driven by one servomotor and one compliant tendon and characterized with single-camera tracking and servo-current sensing. papers.title: Vibration Reduction in a Single-Degree-of-Freedom Flexible Arm via Model Predictive Control and Deep Learning
papers.summary: Single-degree-of-freedom flexible robotic arms are an attractive alternative to rigid manipulators due to their lower mass and energy consumption and greater maneuverability, but their low structural stiffness produces residual vibrations that degrade positioning accuracy. This work presents the experimental implementation of a Model Predictive Controller (MPC) for a single-degree-of-freedom flexible arm, complemented by a Deep Q-Learning (DQN) supervisor that selects online among three weighting profiles of the MPC cost function. papers.title: RoboLab AR: An Augmented Reality Laboratory Environment for Progressive Robotics Education in Latin American Universities
papers.summary: This paper presents RoboLab AR, an open-source desktop robotics laboratory structured into five progressive hands-on practices: fundamental kinematics, custom CAD integration, obstacle-aware motion planning, multibody dynamic control, and physical mockup validation via augmented reality (AR). papers.title: A Methodological Proposal for Developing a Multi-Task Mobile Robot Adapted to Open-Field Agriculture
papers.summary: This paper presents a methodological proposal and a conceptual design framework for developing a multi-task mobile robotic platform tailored for open-field agriculture. Faced with rural demographic crises, population aging, and severe labor shortages in Latin America, open-field automation stands as a vital socio-economic and technological imperative that transcends the limits of traditional greenhouses. papers.title: Efficacy and Prognostic Analysis of Neuro-Navigation Robot-Assisted Puncture Drainage for Thalamic Hemorrhage: A Comparison With Neuro-Endoscopy and External Ventricular Drainage
papers.summary: AIM: This study aims to compare the clinical efficacy of three surgical techniques—robot-assisted neuro-navigation, external ventricular drainage (EVD), and neuro-endoscopy—in evacuating intracranial hematomas in patients with thalamic hemorrhage. METHODS: This retrospective study included 110 patients, divided into three groups based on the surgical method: robot group (n = 30), EVD group (n = 37), and neuro-endoscopy group (n = 43). papers.title: Teknologiskolen robotics camp surveys 2024: de-identified data and analysis code
papers.summary: De-identified data and analysis code for the 2024 surveys of Teknologiskolen's summer robotics camps in Denmark: pre-camp (96 records, 94 in the primary analysis), post-camp (67), helper (13) and approximately three-month follow-up (26) surveys. The files support the article "Supporting learner independence and participation in robotics camps: an exploratory two-cohort study at Teknologiskolen, Denmark" (Frontiers in Education, manuscript 2056684, under review). reproduce.py reproduces the survey results reported in the article. papers.title: LATNAV: A Latency-Aware Real-Time Navigation Framework for Robots in Dynamic Human Environments
papers.summary: In human-populated environments, autonomous service robots are required to navigate safely and efficiently while adhering to stringent real-time constraints. Although recent advancements in deep learning and sensor fusion have significantly enhanced navigation accuracy, many systems regard computational latency as a secondary engineering consideration rather than a primary design variable. papers.title: Confidence-weighted constrained torque allocation for fault-tolerant control of robotic manipulators: A convex projection-based framework
papers.summary: The paper proposes a confidence-weighted constrained torque allocation model of fault-tolerant control (FTC) of robotic manipulators in the presence of actuator degradation and sensor uncertainty. The presented approach develops the redistribution of the torque into a strictly convex quadratic programming (QP) problem including explicit torque magnitude and rate constraints and obtains a global minimum at every sampling instant. A Review of Path Planning Methods for Mobile Robots
papers.summary: Path planning is an indispensable core problem in the autonomous navigation of mobile robots. Whether a safe and efficient trajectory can be planned directly determines the usability of robots in scenarios such as warehousing, delivery, medical assistance and autonomous driving. Scholars at home and abroad have accumulated abundant research results on this problem. Nevertheless, existing methods have respective trade-offs in application scope and performance limits, and no universally recognized optimal solution has been reached so far. papers.title: AFODRLS: an autonomic fog framework for task offloading using deep reinforcement learning with adaptive scheduling
papers.summary: Task offloading in fog computing is difficult because nodes are heterogeneous, workloads are non-stationary, and failures are frequent. Autonomic computing offers self-management through the MAPE-K loop but relies on static rules, and heuristic schedulers degrade under non-stationary or adversarial workloads. Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) is promising, yet studies usually evaluate one algorithm in isolation without statistical validation. papers.title: Intelligent rendering optimization for animated scenes using reinforcement learning and computer vision
papers.summary: Real-time rendering of complex animated scenes is computationally intensive and often struggles to balance visual fidelity and performance in dynamic or densely populated environments, as conventional pipelines lack adaptive resource optimization, leading to reduced frame rates and degraded visual quality. This research proposes an intelligent rendering framework integrating Computer Vision (CV) and Reinforcement Learning (RL) through the Adaptive Seeker-Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (AdapS-Twin D3PG) algorithm. papers.title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Based Financial Portfolio Optimization and Risk Prediction System
papers.summary: Portfolio management under uncertain, non-stationary market conditions is difficult for static allocation methods, which adapt poorly to changing risk. This paper presents a modular multi-agent framework that couples machine-learning-based risk prediction with reinforcement learning (RL) for risk-aware portfolio allocation. Four specialized agents (Market Analysis, Risk Prediction, RL, and Portfolio Optimization) exchange information through a shared coordination interface. papers.title: Electricity Price Aware Production Scheduling with MIP Reinforcement Learning and QUBO An Exploratory Computational Pilot
papers.summary: Purpose Electricity price responsive scheduling can reduce a production electricity bill without reducing physical energy use. This study develops an auditable comparison of a time indexed mixed integer model, a learned dispatch policy and a quadratic unconstrained binary formulation for fixed route job shops. papers.title: Small Language Models as Judges: A Survey
papers.summary: Automated evaluation of language model outputs has shifted from costly human annotation toward model-based judging, yet the field has relied mostly on large proprietary models whose cost, opacity, and data-privacy risks limit scalable deployment. This survey examines Small Language Models (SLMs, ≤14B parameters) as judges, synthesizing 105 works spanning the full pipeline from supervised fine-tuning and preference optimization through reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards to representation-based probing. papers.title: AgentOPSD: Turn-Level Credit Assignment via Recursive Belief Revision
papers.summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards ordinarily spreads a single advantage over a whole trajectory, a granularity too coarse to isolate the few decisions on which success in a long, multi-turn interaction actually turns. Privileged self-distillation supplies denser supervision, but it leaves unanswered how a set of local teacher–student discrepancies should be converted into credit along a sequence.
